page: Vultr vcg-a40-2c-10g-4vram is a fractional GPU instance within the Cloud GPU family. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical Intel core on the x86_64 architecture, running at 2.0 GHz with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 10.0 GB of system memory, providing 5.0 GB per core. For hardware acceleration, it includes a fractional NVIDIA Ampere A40 GPU allocation of approximately 0.0833, which provides 4 GB of dedicated VRAM. Local storage consists of a 180 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear division between CPU-bound operations and GPU-assisted tasks. Single-core CPU performance is average, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1385.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1777.17. However, multi-core CPU and memory bandwidth benchmarks are weak, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 2518.0 and uncached memory read bandwidth at 28.91 GB/sec. Database operations are poor, scoring 956.65 in Passmark. Conversely, the instance demonstrates strong performance in LLM inference prompt processing, achieving 3480.67 tokens/sec for a small 135M model and 202.17 tokens/sec for a medium 7B model.

This instance offers a highly cost-efficient entry point for developers requiring GPU acceleration without the expense of a full dedicated GPU. By slicing the NVIDIA A40 GPU into a 4 GB VRAM profile, Vultr provides a budget-friendly option for lightweight machine learning inference, model prototyping, and small-scale CUDA development. It is not suited for heavy multi-threaded CPU computing, high-throughput database hosting, or large-scale LLM text generation, but fits well for lightweight AI inference, batch image processing, and educational GPU workloads.
